newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe mining shares end week sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe mining shares end week sharply lower.

text.p: Zimbabwe's mining shares slumped 11.76 percent during the week, weakened by volatile trade in Ashanti and a directionless international gold price.
The eight-share index lost 161 points during the week largely due to hefty losses in mining in Ashanti which lost Z$17 on Tuesday and Z$5 on Thursday.
The index finished at 1,207.95 on Friday and has now fallen 358 points or 22.8 percent since setting a high of 1,565 in March this year.
Industrials on the week were quieter, the key index rising to 6,804.52, up 18.51 points or just 0.27 percent, a development brokers attributed to bouts of profit-taking.
Dealers said industrials would remain volatile in the short-term in the absence of fresh direction.
They said, however, that the market could be buoyed by the successful conclusion of talks between the Zimbabwean government and the International Monetary Fund.

"Investors are also waiting for an agreement with the IMF and should this happen the market should go upwards," one said in reference to continuing talks on the second phase of the country's economic strucutral adjustment programme.
